summary: Watched 6 Geography Shorts (plus 2 for their drops) now that retention has arrived; added one lesson, raised one and queued one ending test.
why: Every Short loses most at its second beat (5.4-6.0 s); the steepest falls were a setup line or two figures over an empty frame (Dinorwig -32.4%, English cities -19.1%, Tristan -17.7%), and the two worst Shorts sit 10-11 points under the channel's 59.2% median stayed to watch.

findings.title: Second beat is where viewers leave
findings.detail: All 7 Shorts with drop points fall 15-32% at 5.4-6.0 s. Worst: Dinorwig 32.4% (unknown names, a cave off the map), English cities 19.1% (a tease with no fact), Tristan 17.7% (two distances over an empty sea).

findings.title: Generic first frame cost English cities
findings.detail: Opened on a made-up 'old English city' diagram with no real place named; stayed 48.9% against a 59.2% median.

findings.title: Comment question at the end loses 6-21%
findings.detail: One passport -21.0% at 62.4 s, Sahara -13.2%; queued as challenger geo-loop-no-question.

changes.title: Lesson added: the second line delivers a thing you can see
Lesson raised: the first frame names the subject
changes.detail: now #2, with English cities as the case
